_comment: HOME anchor for live VIVE 2pt teleop. Computed from ONNX default_joint_angles (run 8k8unjkw, model_18500) via the bake FK (bake_motions._load_pinocchio_robot + _compute_vr_fk math). Frame: reference PELVIS, anchor=identity@origin. Order [left, right]. pos = wrist_yaw + R(wrist)@VR_2POINT_OFFSET, expressed pelvis-relative. orn = rot6d C-order [r00,r01,r10,r11,r20,r21] from the wxyz wrist quat. These are BOTH the live calibration target AND the pre-first-WS-message fallback (returning zeros instead would collapse the arms to the pelvis origin).
_comment_3pt: 3-point (exp:g1-wbt-3pt-hybrid) HOME anchor: the SAME two hand points (L,R) PLUS a HEAD point (torso_link + offset (0,0,0.35), pelvis frame). Computed by the SAME bake FK on the SAME default_qpos / URDF (L,R reproduce home_pos_pelvis bit-for-bit — verified). Order [left_wrist_yaw, right_wrist_yaw, torso_link]. orn is RAW xyzw quaternion (3 bodies x 4), NOT the 2pt rot6d — the 3pt policy's vr_3point_orn term is a quaternion. These are the live-3pt calibration target AND the pre-first-message fallback for the head point.
_comment_3pt_tcp: TCP-UNIFIED 3-point anchor (the geometry exp:g1-wbt-3pt-hybrid-unified[-anneal] was retrained on 2026-08-03, e.g. run wda3h4ll): both HAND points sit on the 0.242 m fingertip TCP (== wbt_wrappers_inference.utils.force_deploy_math.TCP_OFFSET_X, the anchor the force stack already acts on) instead of the 0.18 m VR-tracker lever, and the +-0.025 lateral term is DROPPED so position and force supervise ONE point. Mirrors wbt_wrappers_inference.config_values.robot_config.VR_3POINT_OFFSETS_TCP. The HEAD point is carried over UNCHANGED (torso_link +0.35 z) -- it is the same third point in both geometries. Selected by the bridge's --hand-point tcp; the lever arrays above stay the default so every pre-2026-08-03 3pt checkpoint is byte-identical. DERIVATION (not hand-typed): wrist_origin = home_pos_pelvis_3pt[k] - R(home_body_quat_wxyz_3pt[k]) @ vr_3point_offsets[k], then home = wrist_origin + R(quat) @ (0.242,0,0). The resulting per-hand shift is 0.0669 m, which is the documented 6.7 cm/hand TCP-vs-lever gap.
_comment_mc_teleop_5pt_dense: MOTION-COMPLETION teleop HOME fallbacks (bridge --mode 5pt / dense; user 2026-08-27). These are the pre-first-frame values the browser obs classes return, and they are the IDLE_DEFAULT reference pose -- NOT the default_joint_angles pose the 2pt/3pt arrays above use. That difference is deliberate and is 0.289 m / 0.386 in quat: in the MC modes the bridge does NOT anchor on this file at all (its home is Motion_Completion's own 29-joints-ZERO pose, and the wire carries the completion's pelvis-frame keypoints), so there is no bridge anchor to agree with. The right 'hold still' target is then the pose the browser's REFERENCE GHOST holds, which is the injected idle_default clip (arm joints at 0 -- see commit a48662c). DERIVED, not hand-typed: read straight off bake_motions' idle_default.npz (vr5_pos_tcp_local / vr5_orn_local / joint_pos, a 1-frame static clip), and re-derived by tests/test_mc_teleop.py::test_mc_home_fallbacks_are_the_baked_idle_default_pose so they cannot drift from the bake. Slots [0:3] of the position array are bit-identical to the 3pt-TCP prefix of that same bake (asserted), which is what makes 5pt a superset of 3pt.
_comment_mc_dense_home: 58D dense HOME = the idle_default clip's 29 joint targets ++ 29 ZERO velocities, in THAT clip's joint order (which is the policy's -- bake_motions writes joint_names alongside). Velocities are zero because a static hold has none; the live wire supplies finite-differenced ones.
